newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-NEW COACHES BIANCHI AND ANCELOTTI MAKE WINNING STARTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW COACHES BIANCHI AND ANCELOTTI MAKE WINNING STARTS.

text.p: Argentine Carlos Bianchi and ex-Italy international Carlo Ancelotti started their serie A coaching careers in winning style, with Roma and Parma respectively, as Italy's first division kicked off on Saturday.

Bianchi, brought to Roma from Velez of Argentina in the close season, watched his new side see off Piacenza 3-1 at the Olympic stadium with goals from fellow South Americans Aldair of Brazil, Argentine Abel Balbo and Uruguayan Daniel Fonseca.
Ancelotti also made a perfect start on the Parma bench as goals from Dino Baggio and $15 million summer signing Enrico Chiesa put his side two-up in the opening 22 minutes against Napoli.
A superb late effort from Gianfranco Zola, back to his best after the penalty miss that cost Italy elimination from the European Championships, completed a 3-0 thrashing.
The Neapolitan's hopes of a comeback were handicapped by the 42nd dismissal of their Argentine defender Roberto Ayala.
In the other late night match, Swiss playmaker Christian Sforza marked his serie A debut with an eighth minute winner in Inter Milan's 1-0 win at Udinese.

Sforza's goal lifts morale in English coach Roy Hodgson's expensively-assembled side, whose bid for their first title since 1989 was hit last week by news of a heart problem that threatens the career of brilliant young Nigerian Nwankwo Kanu.
Victory will come as some relief to Bianchi whose ability to adapt to serie A was seriously questioned when Roma suffered pre-season elimination from the Italian Cup competition.
The new manager's only anxious moment came in the 49th minute when Pasquale Luiso's penalty briefly threatened to spark a Piacenza fightback.

But Fonseca's 72nd minute third, a tap-in after second-half substitute Francesco Totti saw his shot cannon off keeper Massimo Taibi, assured Roma of the ideal boost ahead of Tuesday's UEFA Cup tie at home to Russia's Dynamo Moscow.

As reward for guiding Reggiana to promotion into the top flight in his first full season of management, Ancelotti was given the difficult task of shaping Parma's rebuilt side into a championship-winning force.
Early elimination from the Italian Cup set alarm bells ringing but on the evidence of Parma's showing against Napoli, the former Milan midfielder is back on course.
As early as the 14th minute, Baggio finished off a sweeping move with a crisp diagonal shot into the corner.
Then, eight minutes later, Chiesa, a prolific striker with Sampdoria and Italy last season, started where he left off, with a fine debut goal, scored from the acutest of angles.
Zola's third was a breathtaking solo effort, a curling shot from 30 metres.

Showing the kind of form that made him a mainstay in Hodgson's Swiss national side, Sforza opened his Italian account by meeting a corner from Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff, another summer signing, with a precise left-foot shot.
Inter started the match with six of their seven foreigners on the field and might have taken a sixth minute lead when Marco Branca saw his shot hit the post.
Udinese came closest to equalising with a diving header from Germany's European Championship hero Oliver Bierhoff, that just missed the target.
In an afternoon match, Bologna, seven-times league champions but languishing in the lower divisions for the past five seasons, celebrated their return to serie A with a 1-0 home win over Lazio.
Davide Fontolan, a summer signing from Internazionale, scored the only goal of the match in the 35th minute, taking advantage of poor defending to head home from close range.
Lazio coach Zdenek Zeman admitted he had erred in keeping prolific striker Giuseppe Signori on the bench for the first-half.
After the break, Signori came on for Igor Protti, equal top scorer with him in serie A last season, and promptly had a header disallowed for a controversial off-side decision.
The match was marred by clashes between rival sets of fans outside the ground before and after the final whistle, with two Lazio supporters taken to hospital with cuts.
